text:
Predicates:
Employees(x) ::: x is an employee.
SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
InCompanyToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
HasLunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
HasLunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
RemotelyFromHome(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
WorksInOtherCountry(x) ::: x works in another country.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James is the individual in question.

Premises:
∀x (SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ∧ Employee(x) → InCompanyToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (HasLunchInCompany(x) → SchedulesMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (HasLunchInCompany(x) ∨ HasLunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or at home.
∀x (HasLunchAtHome(x) → RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (WorksInOtherCountry(x) → RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
James ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
